title: The Abstract Lindenbaum Lemma and Independence via Opposing Completions

problemStatement.formal: \forall\, T : L.\mathrm{Theory},\ T.\mathrm{IsSatisfiable} \Rightarrow \exists\, T' \supseteq T,\ T'.\mathrm{IsComplete};\ \text{and}\ \mathrm{Independent}\,T\,\varphi \Leftrightarrow \exists\, T_1, T_2 \supseteq T,\ T_1.\mathrm{IsComplete} \wedge T_2.\mathrm{IsComplete} \wedge T_1 \models^{b} \varphi \wedge T_2 \models^{b} \neg\varphi.
problemStatement.plain: Prove the Lindenbaum lemma inside Mathlib's first-order model theory: every satisfiable theory extends to a complete one that decides every sentence. Then connect it to independence: a sentence is independent of a theory T exactly when T has two complete extensions that decide it oppositely, one proving the sentence and one proving its negation.
whyMatters: Upgrades the parent entry's satisfiability characterization of independence (both T u {phi} and T u {not phi} satisfiable) to the sharpest completions form: two maximal deciding-everything worlds that split on phi.

The completions view is the model-theoretic heart of every independence result, e.g. the Continuum Hypothesis being independent of ZFC is exactly the existence of two ZFC-completions deciding CH oppositely.
Lindenbaum's lemma is a standard building block toward the Completeness and Compactness theorems, strengthening the reusable model-theory scaffolding around the incompleteness gallery cluster.

proven: independent_iff_satisfiable_both: Independent T phi iff both T u {not phi} and T u {phi} are satisfiable (parent entry godel-incompleteness-oq-03, verified, 0 axioms).

Independent.exists_isComplete_extensions: an independent phi yields two disagreeing complete extensions T1, T2 of T built as complete theories of explicit models (parent entry, verified) -- the forward direction of this problem.
FirstOrder.Language.completeTheory.isComplete: the complete theory of a single structure is complete (Mathlib.ModelTheory.Satisfiability).
FirstOrder.Language.Theory.models_iff_not_satisfiable: the semantic Completeness Theorem bridging unprovability to a model of the negation (Mathlib.ModelTheory.Satisfiability).
open: The general abstract Lindenbaum lemma for an arbitrary satisfiable theory T: every satisfiable T has some complete extension T' containing T.
The full equivalence connecting independence to arbitrary opposing complete extensions, including the reverse direction (two disagreeing completions imply independence).
Whether Mathlib already exposes a Lindenbaum / maximal-consistent-extension lemma directly, or whether it must be assembled from completeTheory of a model plus the Completeness Theorem.
